labels.description: What kind of work the run performed. Deterministic from workload identity; a decision model answers only the residual.

question.instructions: The state describes one Agent Manager run. Classify what kind of work the run performed from workload.kind, harness_kind, run_mode and terminal evidence. Choose the single best option.

options.label: workflow
options.description: One node of a declared workflow execution.

options.label: scheduled
options.description: Work created by a schedule or recurring trigger.

options.label: adhoc
options.description: A one-off run created directly, with no workflow or schedule.

options.label: imported
options.description: A run imported from historical harness transcripts.

labels.description: The run's terminal outcome, preferring the typed terminal pair and falling back to a decision model only when the terminal field is missing.

question.instructions: The state describes one Agent Manager run. Classify its outcome from terminal status, terminal class, stop reason and the last operator/agent exchange. Choose the single best option.

options.label: failed
options.description: The run terminated because the work or executor failed.

options.label: cancelled
options.description: The run stopped on an operator or lifecycle request.

options.label: partial
options.description: Some requested work landed but the run did not complete it.

labels.description: The agent lost significant time finding how or where to act. Optional: about 2 percent of candidate runs in the gold reading, too rare to gate.

question.instructions: Did the agent lose significant time finding the right file, command or syntax before it could act?
question.true_description: Significant time lost discovering the right file, command or contract.
question.false_description: Acted without notable delay in finding the target.

labels.description: A tool, command or service error, refusal, rate limit or outage stopped the agent from finishing or verifying a required step. A test or review that correctly reports a defect does not count. Existing tool findings are the prior. Optional (skipped unless asked for) since the bake-off: every measured model of 512 to 1024 tokens answers at chance on the hold-out (fitted temperature at its cap of 20, hold-out precision 0.33 at best), the 8192-token models could not be loaded, and a rule over the failure counters scored precision 0.75 and recall 0.27 on the hold-out. Re-enable after a model with the context to read the agent's text, or a digest that keeps it, is measured (notes/J2-bakeoff.md).

question.instructions: Did a tool, command or service error, refusal, rate limit or outage stop the agent from finishing or verifying a required step?
question.true_description: Blocked: an error, refusal, rate limit or outage stopped a required step.
question.false_description: Not blocked: a test or review that correctly reports a defect is not a tool failure.

labels.description: The operator's own message shows dissatisfaction with, or pushback on, the agent's work, pace or progress, mildly or strongly. Mild pushback is most of what operators write (34 of 49 gold positives; 7 are plain anger), so the label is named for it. A specific defect report, a design preference, a plain question or praise with a small note is not dissatisfaction. One answer per human message.

question.instructions: Is the operator dissatisfied with the agent's work or pace?
question.true_description: Dissatisfied: criticises or pushes back on the work, mildly or strongly.
question.false_description: Not dissatisfied: neutral, thanks or instructing.

labels.description: The operator's own message shows satisfaction, praise or approval of the agent's work. One answer per human message.

question.instructions: Does the operator praise the work or say they are pleased?
question.false_description: Not pleased: neutral, critical or instructing.

labels.description: The operator's own message pushes the agent to hurry, wrap up or stop stalling. One answer per human message.

question.instructions: Is the operator pressing the agent to hurry, wrap up or stop stalling?
question.true_description: Impatient: hurry, wrap up, or stop stalling.
question.false_description: Not impatient: ordinary request, plain continue or feedback.

labels.description: How the operator's own message leans: pleased minus dissatisfied, from the two message labels. Derived, never asked; positive is pleased, negative is dissatisfied.

The share of the run's human messages that showed dissatisfaction: the mean calibrated probability over the run's dissatisfied messages, so it does not rise with how many messages the run has (a maximum did: 0 of 6 runs with two messages or fewer scored positive against 15 of 19 with three or more). Derived from operator.dissatisfied, never asked. The search and friction thresholds are declared, not measured: about twice the message-level base rate in gold (11 percent).

question.instructions: What share of the operator's messages in this run showed dissatisfaction?
question.true_description: A large share of the messages were dissatisfied.
question.false_description: Few or none of the messages were dissatisfied.

labels.description: The share of the run's human messages that showed praise or satisfaction: the mean calibrated probability over the run's pleased messages, so it does not rise with how many messages the run has (a maximum did: 0 of 6 runs with two messages or fewer scored positive against 15 of 19 with three or more). Derived from operator.pleased, never asked. The search and friction thresholds are declared, not measured: about twice the message-level base rate in gold (12 percent).

question.instructions: What share of the operator's messages in this run showed praise or satisfaction?
question.true_description: A large share of the messages were pleased.

Derived from operator.impatient, never asked. The search and friction thresholds are declared, not measured: about twice the message-level base rate in gold (6 percent).
